We need a retrosynthesis route with at most 1 step (i.e., direct synthesis from commercially available chemicals). Leaves must be commercially available and total price <=125. Need to propose a reaction template and precursors.

Target: COC(C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2)=O. This is methyl ester of a keto? Actually it's methyl ester of a carbonyl attached to a cyclopropyl? Let's parse: COC( ... )=O is methyl ester of a carbonyl attached to a quaternary carbon bearing a cyclopropyl? Wait: COC( ... )=O is methyl ester of a carboxylate: OCH3 attached to C=O. The carbonyl carbon attached to C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=... So it's a carbonyl attached to a cyclopropyl with a phenyl vinyl and TMS group.

Probably can be made via esterification of the corresponding acid: OC(=O)C1(C=C1[Si](C)(C)C)/C=C/C2=CC=CC=C2 (the acid). So we need acid and methanol (or methylating agent). But we need 1 step only, so maybe direct esterification using Fischer esterification with methanol (commercial) and acid (commercial). Need both commercially available and total price <=125.

Check if the acid is commercially available. Search.
